claim: Marburg virus (MARV) is one of the filovirus species that cause deadly hemorrhagic fever in humans, with mortality rates up to 90%.
source: Marburg virus (MARV) is one of the filovirus species that cause deadly hemorrhagic fever in humans, with mortality rates up to 90%.
evidence: This is a well-established fact about MARV cited in the abstract and introduction, representing established scientific knowledge about the virus.

claim: No antibody has been approved for MARV treatment to date.
source: However, no antibody has been approved for MARV treatment to date.
evidence: This statement reflects the current state of approved therapeutics, representing established knowledge in the field.

claim: AF-03 is a novel human antibody that targets MARV glycoprotein (GP).
source: In this study, we identified a novel human antibody named AF-03 that targeted MARV glycoprotein (GP).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: AF-03 possesses a high binding affinity to MARV GP.
source: AF-03 possessed a high binding affinity to MARV GP and showed neutralizing and protective activities against the pseudotyped MARV in vitro and in vivo.
evidence: This claim is supported by ELISA and SPR data showing binding affinity measurements.

claim: AF-03 shows neutralizing and protective activities against pseudotyped MARV in vitro and in vivo.
source: AF-03 possessed a high binding affinity to MARV GP and showed neutralizing and protective activities against the pseudotyped MARV in vitro and in vivo.
evidence: This is supported by neutralization assays in cell culture and mouse protection experiments presented in the results.

claim: AF-03 recognizes the Niemann-Pick C1 (NPC1) binding domain within GP1.
source: Epitope identification, including molecular docking and experiment-based analysis of mutated species, revealed that AF-03 recognized the Niemann-Pick C1 (NPC1) binding domain within GP1.
evidence: This is supported by molecular docking studies and mutagenesis experiments showing loss of binding/neutralization with specific mutations.

claim: AF-03 has neutralizing activity against pseudotyped Ebola viruses (EBOV, SUDV, and BDBV) harboring cleaved GP instead of full-length GP.
source: Interestingly, we found the neutralizing activity of AF-03 to pseudotyped Ebola viruses (EBOV, SUDV, and BDBV) harboring cleaved GP instead of full-length GP.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing differential neutralization of thermolysin-treated versus untreated pseudoviruses.

claim: NPC2-fused AF-03 exhibits neutralizing activity to several filovirus species and EBOV mutants via binding to CI-MPR.
source: Furthermore, NPC2-fused AF-03 exhibited neutralizing activity to several filovirus species and EBOV mutants via binding to CI-MPR.
evidence: This is supported by neutralization data with AF03-NL and experiments showing CI-MPR dependence through knockdown and overexpression studies.

claim: Filoviruses are nonsegmented negative-sense RNA viruses, comprised of six genera.
source: Filoviruses are nonsegmented negative-sense RNA viruses, comprised of six genera, Ebolavirus, Marburgvirus, Cuevavirus, Striavirus, Thamnovirus, and a recently discovered sixth genus, Dianlovirus (Amarasinghe et al., 2019; Baseler et al., 2017; Kuhn et al., 2019).
evidence: This is established knowledge about filovirus taxonomy supported by citations to the literature.

claim: The Marburgvirus genus consists of Marburg virus (MARV) and Ravn virus (RAVN).
source: The Marburgvirus genus consists of Marburg virus (MARV) and Ravn virus (RAVN) (Amarasinghe et al., 2019; Bào et al., 2017; Ristanović et al., 2020).
evidence: This is established taxonomic knowledge supported by citations.

claim: MARV includes three strains: Uganda, Angola, and Musoke.
source: The former includes three strains-- Uganda, Angola, and Musoke.
evidence: This is established knowledge about MARV strain classification.

claim: The Ebola virus genus includes six distinct species including Zaire Ebola virus (EBOV), Bundibugyo virus (BDBV), Sudan virus (SUDV), Reston virus (RESTV), Taii Forest virus (TAFV) and Bombali virus (BOMV).
source: The Ebola virus genus includes six distinct species including Zaire Ebola virus (EBOV), Bundibugyo virus (BDBV), Sudan virus (SUDV), Reston virus (RESTV), Taii Forest virus (TAFV) and Bombali virus (BOMV), the first three of which cause severe hemorrhagic fevers (Fan et al., 2020; Goldstein et al., 2018).
evidence: This is established taxonomic knowledge supported by citations.

claim: EBOV, BDBV, and SUDV cause severe hemorrhagic fevers.
source: The Ebola virus genus includes six distinct species including Zaire Ebola virus (EBOV), Bundibugyo virus (BDBV), Sudan virus (SUDV), Reston virus (RESTV), Taii Forest virus (TAFV) and Bombali virus (BOMV), the first three of which cause severe hemorrhagic fevers (Fan et al., 2020; Goldstein et al., 2018).
evidence: This is established knowledge about disease-causing Ebola species supported by citations.

claim: Cuevavirus (Lloviu virus, LLOV) was isolated from Miniopterus schreibersii bats in Spain and Hungary.
source: The genus Cuevavirus (Lloviu virus, LLOV) was isolated from Miniopterus schreibersii bats in Spain and Hungary and potently infected monkeys and human cells (Negredo et al., 2011; Kemenesi et al., 2022).
evidence: This is established knowledge about LLOV supported by citations.

claim: LLOV potently infected monkeys and human cells.
source: The genus Cuevavirus (Lloviu virus, LLOV) was isolated from Miniopterus schreibersii bats in Spain and Hungary and potently infected monkeys and human cells (Negredo et al., 2011; Kemenesi et al., 2022).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Měnglà virus (MLAV) was discovered in the liver of a bat from Mengla, Yunnan, China in 2019.
source: The genus Měnglà virus (MLAV) was discovered in the liver of a bat from Mengla, Yunnan, China in 2019.
evidence: This is established knowledge about MLAV discovery supported by citation.

claim: Only an almost complete RNA sequence of the MLAV viral genome is available, with no viable MLAVs isolated.
source: So far, only an almost complete RNA sequence of the viral genome is available, there are no viable MLAVs isolated (Yang et al., 2019).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the current state of MLAV research supported by citation.

claim: MARV and EBOV infect humans and non-human primates.
source: MARV and EBOV infect humans and non-human primates, causing Marburg virus disease (MVD) and EBOV virus disease (EVD) with an incubation period of 2–21 days (Mehedi et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge about host range supported by citation.

claim: MARV and EBOV cause Marburg virus disease (MVD) and EBOV virus disease (EVD) with an incubation period of 2–21 days.
source: MARV and EBOV infect humans and non-human primates, causing Marburg virus disease (MVD) and EBOV virus disease (EVD) with an incubation period of 2–21 days (Mehedi et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established clinical knowledge supported by citation.

claim: The symptoms of MVD include severe headache and high fever rapidly within 5 days of the onset of symptoms, followed by diarrhea and vomiting, leading to up to 90% fatality rate.
source: The symptoms of MVD include severe headache and high fever rapidly within 5 days of the onset of symptoms, followed by diarrhea and vomiting, leading to up to 90% fatality rate (Mehedi et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established clinical knowledge about MVD symptoms supported by citation.

claim: Glycoprotein (GP) on the surface of filoviruses is a type I transmembrane protein and consists of GP1 and GP2 subunits.
source: Glycoprotein (GP) on the surface of filoviruses is a type I transmembrane protein and consists of GP1 and GP2 subunits (Beniac and Booth, 2017; Lee and Saphire, 2009).
evidence: This is established structural knowledge about filovirus GP supported by citations.

claim: Filovirus GP is inserted into the virus envelope in the form of homotrimeric spikes.
source: It is inserted into the virus envelope in the form of homotrimeric spikes (Brauburger et al., 2012) and is responsible for viral attachment and entry.
evidence: This is established structural knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Filovirus GP is responsible for viral attachment and entry.
source: It is inserted into the virus envelope in the form of homotrimeric spikes (Brauburger et al., 2012) and is responsible for viral attachment and entry.
evidence: This is established functional knowledge about GP.

claim: Furin cleaves Marburg GP at amino acid 435 into two subunits, GP1 and GP2, which remain linked by a disulfide bond.
source: The furin cleaves Marburg GP at the amino acid 435 into two subunits, GP1 and GP2, which remain linked by a disulfide bond (Schafer et al., 2021).
evidence: This is established knowledge about GP processing supported by citation.

claim: GP1 contains a receptor binding domain (RBD), a glycan cap, and a heavily glycosylated mucin-like domain (MLD).
source: GP1 contains a receptor binding domain (RBD), a glycan cap, and a heavily glycosylated mucin-like domain (MLD), which mediates binding to entry factors and receptors (Hashiguchi et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established structural knowledge about GP1 supported by citation.

claim: GP1 mediates binding to entry factors and receptors.
source: GP1 contains a receptor binding domain (RBD), a glycan cap, and a heavily glycosylated mucin-like domain (MLD), which mediates binding to entry factors and receptors (Hashiguchi et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established functional knowledge supported by citation.

claim: GP2 has a partial MLD, a transmembrane domain for viral anchoring to the envelope surface, and a fusion peptide required for the fusion of virus and cell membranes.
source: GP2 has a partial MLD, a transmembrane domain for viral anchoring to the envelop surface, and a fusion peptide required for the fusion of virus and cell membranes (Fusco et al., 2015; Gregory et al., 2011; Lee et al., 2017).
evidence: This is established structural and functional knowledge about GP2 supported by citations.

claim: In the Ebola virus, the furin cleavage site is located at residue 501 and the entire MLD is attached to the GP1 subunit.
source: In the Ebola virus, the furin cleavage site is located at residue 501 and the entire MLD is attached to the GP1 subunit (Volchkov et al., 2000).
evidence: This is established structural knowledge about EBOV GP supported by citation.

claim: Marburg virus contains 66 amino acids on GP2 that are absent from the Ebola virus MLD, called 'wings' due to their outward projection and flexibility.
source: Marburg virus contains 66 amino acids on GP2 that are absent from the Ebola virus MLD, and are called 'wings' due to their outward projection and flexibility (Fusco et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established structural knowledge about MARV GP supported by citation.

claim: GP is a major target for antibodies validated in filovirus-infected animals and clinical trials.
source: Currently, GP is a major target for antibodies validated in filovirus-infected animals and clinical trials because it is exposed on the surface of the virus and plays a key role in viral entry (Dye et al., 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge about therapeutic development supported by citation.

claim: GP is exposed on the surface of the virus and plays a key role in viral entry.
source: Currently, GP is a major target for antibodies validated in filovirus-infected animals and clinical trials because it is exposed on the surface of the virus and plays a key role in viral entry (Dye et al., 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge about GP function supported by citation.

claim: Filoviruses initially enter cells by endocytosis or macropinocytosis.
source: Filoviruses initially enter cells by endocytosis or macropinocytosis (Aleksandrowicz et al., 2011; Saeed et al., 2010).
evidence: This is established knowledge about viral entry mechanisms supported by citations.

claim: Once inside the endosome, GP is cleaved by host cathepsins, and glycan cap and MLD are removed, enabling GP to bind to NPC1.
source: Once inside the endosome, GP is cleaved by host cathepsins, and glycan cap and MLD are removed, enabling GP to bind to NPC1 (Carette et al., 2011; Brecher et al., 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the viral entry mechanism supported by citations.

claim: Ebola viral entry requires cathepsin B cleavage.
source: Interestingly, Ebola viral entry requires cathepsin B cleavage (Martinez et al., 2010), which is redundant for MARV entry (Gnirss et al., 2012; Misasi et al., 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge about EBOV entry supported by citation.

claim: Cathepsin B cleavage is redundant for MARV entry.
source: Interestingly, Ebola viral entry requires cathepsin B cleavage (Martinez et al., 2010), which is redundant for MARV entry (Gnirss et al., 2012; Misasi et al., 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge about MARV entry supported by citations.

claim: The receptor binding domain is masked by glycan cap and MLD in the Ebola virus, whereas it is partially exposed in the Marburg virus.
source: Hashiguchi et al., 2015 proposed that the receptor binding domain was masked by glycan cap and MLD in the Ebola virus, whereas it was partially exposed in the Marburg virus.
evidence: This is knowledge from the literature supported by citation.

claim: There is no licensed treatment or vaccine for Marburg infection.
source: To date, there is no licensed treatment or vaccine for Marburg infection, although a panel of antibodies with the potentials of neutralization has been isolated from a survivor subjected to MARV infection (Flyak et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the current state of MARV therapeutics.

claim: A panel of antibodies with neutralization potential has been isolated from a survivor subjected to MARV infection.
source: To date, there is no licensed treatment or vaccine for Marburg infection, although a panel of antibodies with the potentials of neutralization has been isolated from a survivor subjected to MARV infection (Flyak et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge from the literature supported by citation.

claim: AF-03 was selected from a well-established phage surface display antibody library with immense diversity in the selected complementarity determining region (CDR) loops.
source: AF-03 was selected from a well-established phage surface display antibody library with immense diversity in the selected complementarity determining region (CDR) loops (Liu et al., 2021; Duan et al., 2019).
evidence: This describes the methodology used to identify AF-03, supported by citations to previous work.

claim: AF-03 was eukaryotically expressed with purity over 95%.
source: As shown in Figure 1A, AF-03 was eukaryotically expressed with the purity of over 95%.
evidence: This is supported by SDS-PAGE data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: ELISA analysis showed remarkable binding of AF-03 to MARV GP.
source: ELISA analysis showed the remarkable binding of AF-03 to MARV GP (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: AF-03 bound to MARV GP with a KD value of 4.71 × 10–11 M.
source: Furthermore, SPR assay was done to determine the binding kinetics and showed that AF-03 bound to MARV GP with high affinity (AF-03 KD value was 4.71 × 10–11 M, monovalent AF-03 Fab KD value was 2.15 × 10–11 M) (Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by SPR data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Monovalent AF-03 Fab bound to MARV GP with a KD value of 2.15 × 10–11 M.
source: Furthermore, SPR assay was done to determine the binding kinetics and showed that AF-03 bound to MARV GP with high affinity (AF-03 KD value was 4.71 × 10–11 M, monovalent AF-03 Fab KD value was 2.15 × 10–11 M) (Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by SPR data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Q128S-N129S or C226Y mutation significantly impaired the neutralizing activity of AF-03 to MARV pseudovirus compared with WT MARV.
source: The inhibition assay revealed the significant impairment of the neutralizing activity of AF-03 to MARV pseudovirus harboring Q128S-N129S or C226Y compared with WT MARV and those loading other indicated mutations (Figure 2A left panel), which indicates that Q128/N129/C226 functions as key amino acids responsible for AF-03 neutralization.
evidence: This is supported by neutralization assay data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Q128/N129/C226 functions as key amino acids responsible for AF-03 neutralization.
source: The inhibition assay revealed the significant impairment of the neutralizing activity of AF-03 to MARV pseudovirus harboring Q128S-N129S or C226Y compared with WT MARV and those loading other indicated mutations (Figure 2A left panel), which indicates that Q128/N129/C226 functions as key amino acids responsible for AF-03 neutralization.
evidence: This is inferred from the mutagenesis data showing loss of neutralization with these specific mutations.

claim: Q128S-N129S or C226Y mutation significantly disrupted the binding of GP to AF-03.
source: Furthermore, we constructed the mutated MARV GP. ELISA assay showed that Q128S-N129S or C226Y mutation significantly disrupted the binding of GP to AF-03, while the binding and neutralizing capacity of MR78 to mutant GP and pseudovirus harboring C226Y instead of Q128S-N129S, a mAb reported to be isolated from Marburg virus survivors (Hashiguchi et al., 2015), was comparable to WT counterparts (Figure 2A right panel and B).
evidence: This is supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The binding and neutralizing capacity of MR78 to mutant GP and pseudovirus harboring C226Y was comparable to WT counterparts.
source: Furthermore, we constructed the mutated MARV GP. ELISA assay showed that Q128S-N129S or C226Y mutation significantly disrupted the binding of GP to AF-03, while the binding and neutralizing capacity of MR78 to mutant GP and pseudovirus harboring C226Y instead of Q128S-N129S, a mAb reported to be isolated from Marburg virus survivors (Hashiguchi et al., 2015), was comparable to WT counterparts (Figure 2A right panel and B).
evidence: This is supported by ELISA and neutralization data shown in Figure 2A and 2B.

claim: The structure of both mutants (Q128S-N129S and C226Y) was not obviously different from that of the parental GP by circular dichroism.
source: Furthermore, we analyzed the secondary structure of the MARV GP and its mutants. By circular dichroism, the structure of both mutants was not obviously different from that of the parental GP (Figure 2C and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is supported by circular dichroism data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The weakened binding to the antibody was not due to the conformational change of GP caused by the mutation.
source: Therefore, the weakened binding to the antibody was not due to the conformational change of GP caused by the mutation.
evidence: This is inferred from the circular dichroism data showing no structural changes in the mutants.

claim: AF-03 and MR78 could compete with each other to bind to MARV GP.
source: Competitive ELISA showed that AF-03 and MR78 could compete with each other to bind to MARV GP (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is supported by competitive ELISA data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The epitopes of AF-03 and MR78 overlapped partially.
source: Collectively, these results indicate the epitopes of these two mAbs overlapped partially.
evidence: This is inferred from the competitive binding data.

claim: Liver and adrenal glands have been reported to be the early targets of MARV infection.
source: Liver and adrenal glands have been reported to be the early targets of MARV infection (Brauburger et al., 2012; Shifflett and Marzi, 2019).
evidence: This is established knowledge from the literature supported by citations.

claim: Huh7 and HEK293T cell lines were susceptible to MARV cell entry.
source: Therefore, we first tested the entry of MARV to hepatocyte cell line (Huh7) and renal cell line (HEK293T cells) by measuring the relative luciferase intensity. These two cell lines were susceptible to MARV cell entry.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing viral entry in these cell lines.

claim: AF-03 actively inhibited pseudotyped MARV viral entry to HEK293T cells, with IC50 value of 0.13 μg/ml.
source: In contrast, AF-03 actively inhibited viral entry to HEK293T cells, with IC50 value of 0.13 μg/ml. As well, IC50 of MR78 was 0.44 μg/ml (Figure 3A left panel).
evidence: This is supported by neutralization assay data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: IC50 of MR78 for inhibiting MARV entry to HEK293T cells was 0.44 μg/ml.
source: In contrast, AF-03 actively inhibited viral entry to HEK293T cells, with IC50 value of 0.13 μg/ml. As well, IC50 of MR78 was 0.44 μg/ml (Figure 3A left panel).
evidence: This is supported by neutralization assay data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: In Huh7 cells, IC50 of AF-03 and MR78 was 0.4 and 1.03 μg/ml, respectively.
source: In Huh7 cells, IC50 of AF-03 and MR78 was 0.4 and 1.03 μg/ml, respectively (Figure 3A right panel).
evidence: This is supported by neutralization assay data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: AF-03 has a stronger potency of neutralization than MR78.
source: These results suggest that AF-03 has a stronger potency of neutralization than MR78.
evidence: This is inferred from the comparison of IC50 values between AF-03 and MR78.

claim: AF-03 showed strong and comparable neutralizing ability to pseudotyped Angola, Musoke, and RAVN strains with IC50 of 0.32, 0.12, and 0.15 μg/ml, respectively.
source: We also conducted AF-03 neutralization experiments on pseudotyped Angola, Musoke, and RAVN strains and showed a strong and comparable neutralizing ability to all these strains (IC50 was 0.32, 0.12, and 0.15 μg/ml, respectively) (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is supported by neutralization assay data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The AF-03-treated group displayed lower bioluminescence activity compared with the control group in mice exposed to pseudotyped MARV.
source: As shown in Figure 3C and D, the AF-03-treated group displayed lower bioluminescence activity compared with the control group, while the treatment with control antibodies had no effects.
evidence: This is supported by in vivo bioluminescence imaging data shown in Figure 3C and 3D.

claim: Administration of 1 mg/kg AF-03 prior to the injection of MARV could decrease viral infection to approximately 50% level.
source: Administration of 1 mg/kg AF-03 prior to the injection of MARV could decrease viral infection to approximately 50% level and increasing doses of AF-03 led to higher preventive efficacy.
evidence: This is supported by in vivo bioluminescence data.

claim: Increasing doses of AF-03 led to higher preventive efficacy against MARV infection.
source: Administration of 1 mg/kg AF-03 prior to the injection of MARV could decrease viral infection to approximately 50% level and increasing doses of AF-03 led to higher preventive efficacy.
evidence: This is supported by dose-response data from in vivo experiments.

claim: AF-03 is capable of preventing MARV infection in a dose-dependent manner.
source: This indicates clearly that AF-03 is capable of preventing from MARV infection in a dose-dependent manner and represents a potential candidate for MARV treatment.
evidence: This is inferred from the dose-response data in the in vivo experiments.

claim: Glycan cap or mucin-like domain are known to mask the putative receptor-binding domain on EBOV, SUDV, and BDBV GP.
source: In addition, considering that glycan cap or mucin-like domain are known to mask the putative receptor-binding domain on EBOV, SUDV, and BDBV GP and thus impede the engagement between AF-03 and GP (Hashiguchi et al., 2015), glycan cap and mucin-like domain were enzymatically cleaved by digesting GP with 250 μg/ml thermolysin at 37 °C.
evidence: This is established knowledge from the literature supported by citation.

claim: The infection of pseudotyped ebolavirus harboring cleaved GP to host cells was comparable or stronger than those containing intact GP.
source: The infection of pseudotyped ebolavirus harboring cleaved GP to host cells was comparable or stronger than those containing intact GP (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by infection data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The inhibitory function of AF-03 on cell entry of EBOV, SUDV, and BDBV bearing cleaved GP was much stronger than those bearing uncleaved GP.
source: Intriguingly, the inhibitory function of AF-03 on cell entry of all three species of ebolavirus bearing cleaved GP was much stronger than those bearing uncleaved GP (Figure 4), which suggests that AF-03 has therapeutic potentials for EBOV, SUDV, and BDBV infection.
evidence: This is supported by neutralization data comparing cleaved versus uncleaved GP shown in Figure 4.

claim: AF-03 has therapeutic potentials for EBOV, SUDV, and BDBV infection.
source: Intriguingly, the inhibitory function of AF-03 on cell entry of all three species of ebolavirus bearing cleaved GP was much stronger than those bearing uncleaved GP (Figure 4), which suggests that AF-03 has therapeutic potentials for EBOV, SUDV, and BDBV infection.
evidence: This is inferred from the neutralization data showing activity against cleaved GP forms.

claim: NPC2-fused AF-03 (AF03-NL), rather than AF-03, bound to CI-MPR1-3.
source: The results showed that NPC2-fused AF-03 (termed AF03-NL), rather than AF-03, bound to CI-MPR1-3 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: AF03-NL instead of AF-03 adhered to the cell surface of HEK293T cells expressing CI-MPR.
source: As expected, AF03-NL instead of AF-03 adhered to the cell surface, detected by fluorescence-labelled secondary IgG.
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data showing cell surface binding.

claim: Upon endocytosis, the fluorescence on the cell surface decreased dramatically, implying the occurrence of AF03-NL internalization.
source: Upon endocytosis, the fluorescence on the cell surface decreased dramatically, implying the occurrence of AF03-NL internalization (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: APC and pHrodo Red-conjugated AF03-NL was observed in the acidic endosomal compartment by flow cytometry and fluorescence microscopy.
source: Consequently, APC and pHrodo Red-conjugated AF03-NL was observed in the acidic endosomal compartment by flow cytometry and fluorescence microscopy, respectively (Figure 5B and C).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry and microscopy data shown in Figure 5B and 5C.

claim: AF-03 was not seen in the endosome.
source: In contrast, AF-03 was not seen in the endosome.
evidence: This is supported by the absence of signal in flow cytometry and microscopy experiments.

claim: AF03-NL showed stronger neutralizing activity than AF-03 against MARV pseudovirus with IC50 of 0.057 and 0.284 μg/ml, respectively.
source: Intriguingly, AF03-NL showed stronger neutralizing activity than AF-03 (The IC50 was 0.057 and 0.284 μg/ml, respectively) (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B), which may be attributed to sustained tethering of AF03-NL to pseudovirus at extracellular space as well as endosomal compartment.
evidence: This is supported by neutralization assay data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The stronger neutralizing activity of AF03-NL may be attributed to sustained tethering to pseudovirus at extracellular space as well as endosomal compartment.
source: Intriguingly, AF03-NL showed stronger neutralizing activity than AF-03 (The IC50 was 0.057 and 0.284 μg/ml, respectively) (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B), which may be attributed to sustained tethering of AF03-NL to pseudovirus at extracellular space as well as endosomal compartment.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the observed enhanced neutralization.

claim: AF03-NL displayed superior neutralizing activity to nine filovirus species compared to AF-03.
source: Second, we compared the neutralizing activity of AF03-NL and AF-03 to a series of filovirus species. AF03-NL displayed superior neutralizing activity to the other nine filovirus species. While, no or weak inhibition of entry by AF-03 was found (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is supported by neutralization data across multiple filovirus species shown in Figure 6A.

claim: AF03-NL, instead of AF-03, actively inhibited cell entry of 17 EBOV mutants that were detected previously in natural hosts.
source: Furthermore, AF03-NL, instead of AF-03, also actively inhibited cell entry of 17 EBOV mutants that were detected previously in natural hosts (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is supported by neutralization data for EBOV mutants shown in Figure 6B.

claim: AF-03, NPC2 alone or in combination did not inhibit EBOV entry.
source: AF-03, NPC2 alone or in combination did not inhibit EBOV entry. Conversely, AF03-NL actively impeded this process (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is supported by neutralization assay data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: AF03-NL actively impeded EBOV entry.
source: AF-03, NPC2 alone or in combination did not inhibit EBOV entry. Conversely, AF03-NL actively impeded this process (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is supported by neutralization assay data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: CI-MPR knockdown rendered significant abrogation of the inhibitory ability of AF03-NL.
source: The result showed that CI-MPR knockdown rendered significant abrogation of the inhibitory ability of AF03-NL (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is supported by neutralization data in CI-MPR knockdown cells shown in Figure 7C.

claim: The inhibitory effects of AF03-NL were augmented in CI-MPR-overexpressed cells compared with empty vector-introduced counterparts.
source: We also introduced CI-MPR into the Huh7 cell line that is null for this receptor (Figure 5—figure supplement 2B). The inhibitory effects of AF03-NL were augmented in CI-MPR-overexpressed cells compared with empty vector-introduced counterparts (Figure 7D).
evidence: This is supported by neutralization data in CI-MPR overexpressing cells shown in Figure 7D.

claim: The inhibitory potency of AF03-NL is dependent on the interaction between NPC2 and CI-MPR.
source: Taken together, these data indicate that the inhibitory potency of AF03-NL is dependent on the interaction between NPC2 and CI-MPR.
evidence: This is inferred from the knockdown and overexpression experiments showing CI-MPR dependence.

claim: The Marburg virus was initially identified after simultaneous outbreaks in Marburg and Frankfurt in Germany in 1967.
source: The Marburg virus was initially identified after simultaneous outbreaks in Marburg and Frankfurt in Germany in 1967 (Hashiguchi et al., 2015; Abir et al., 2022).
evidence: This is established historical knowledge supported by citations.

claim: There have been a dozen outbreaks of Marburg virus infection in humans to date.
source: To date, there have been a dozen outbreaks of Marburg virus infection in humans (Araf et al., 2023).
evidence: This is established epidemiological knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Several MARV GP-specific neutralizing antibodies were screened from the PBMC samples of a MARV-infected survivor, which achieved 100% protection in mice subjected to mouse-adapted MARV challenge.
source: Flyak et al., 2015 screened several MARV GP-specific neutralizing antibodies from the PBMC samples of a MARV-infected survivor, which achieved 100% protection in mice subjected to mouse-adapted MARV challenge.
evidence: This is established knowledge from the literature supported by citation.

claim: Three mAbs cocktail could protect hamsters from lethal hamster-adapted MARV infection, while treatment with either one or two antibodies failed.
source: The MARV GP-specific antibody cocktail was also developed, three mAbs cocktail could protect hamsters from lethal hamster-adapted MARV infection, while treatment with either one or two antibodies failed (Marzi et al., 2018).
evidence: This is established knowledge from the literature supported by citation.

claim: AF-03 effectively inhibited HIV vector pseudotyped MARV viral entry at IC50 of 0.13 and 0.4 μg/ml in HEK293T and Huh7, respectively.
source: The results showed that AF-03 effectively inhibited HIV vector (pSG3.Δenv.cmvFluc) pseudotyped MARV viral entry at IC50 of 0.13 and 0.4 μg/ml in HEK293T and Huh7, respectively.
evidence: This is supported by neutralization assay data presented in the results.

claim: Compared with the control antibody, AF-03 exhibited a protective property against pseudovirus infection in mice.
source: Furthermore, compared with the control antibody, AF-03 exhibited a protective property against pseudovirus infection in mice.
evidence: This is supported by in vivo bioluminescence data.

claim: N129 is known to be located in the NPC1 binding domain.
source: Epitope mapping results showed that Q128-N129 and C226 of GP was the binding and functional epitopes that interacted with AF-03, which means AF-03 targeting the interface of GP-NPC1 interaction, considering that N129 is known to be located in the NPC1 binding domain.
evidence: This is established structural knowledge about GP.

claim: RBD is highly conserved among filovirus species.
